title: Graceful probe quarantine and priority-based request drain to stabilize autoscaling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Intermittent probe flaps (short-lived readiness failures) cause aggressive autoscaler churn in production. Churn manifests as repeated scale-down/scale-up cycles and reactive load shedding that violates our P95 latency SLOs in secondary regions. Goal: Implement a probe quarantine pattern plus a priority-aware request drain so nodes with transient probe failures are isolated without triggering full autoscaler reactivity, and lower-priority traffic is shed before latency-critical traffic during resource pressure.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a quarantine state for instances that fail N readiness checks within a short window, with staged isolation duration configurable per deployment
Quarantined instances are removed from SLO-sensitive routing pools but retained for background warmup/diagnostics and can be reintroduced after health stabilization
Request router supports priority buckets (high/normal/low) and drains low-priority requests from candidate nodes during an out-of-capacity signal
Autoscaler metrics show reduced thrash: 80% reduction in scale-up/scale-down events attributable to probe flaps in the canary region during a 2-week experiment
End-to-end playbook for multi-region failover ensures circuit breakers prefer healthy regions while quarantined instances are observed but not used for primary traffic
No new P95 latency regressions in synthetic and production traffic during phased rollout
tasks: Design probe quarantine lifecycle (thresholds, backoff, quarantine TTL, reintroduction policy)
Extend readiness controller to emit quarantine signals and attach metadata to instance records
Add priority-aware drain hooks to the edge router: mark a node as suitable only for high/normal/low buckets
Update autoscaler hysteresis rules to treat quarantined instances as neutral for scale decisions for a configurable window
Create observability dashboards: quarantine count, quarantine latency, per-priority drop rates, autoscale event attribution
Write integration tests and chaos scenarios that simulate probe flaps, network blips, and node GC pauses
Run staged canary in staging, then eu-west-1 (secondary region) for two weeks before global rollout
decisions: Quarantine TTL default: 90s with exponential backoff for repeated failures (configurable per service)
Quarantined instances continue to serve background prefetched traffic for cache-warmth, but are excluded from SLO-tagged routing
Request priorities: high=latency-sensitive, normal=interactive, low=batch/retryable. Default mapping is service-level configurable
Autoscaler change: treat quarantined instances as neither fully healthy nor failed; they will not drive scale-down but can contribute to capacity calculations after a probation window
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flags + unit tests merged to main (small internal services)
Phase 1: Staging deployment + chaos engineering run (probe flaps simulated) - monitor dashboards
Phase 2: Canary in eu-west-1 for low-traffic team, 14-day observation window
Phase 3: Expand to additional secondary regions and increase sample size; enable priority drain on edge routers
Phase 4: Global enable for non-critical services, observe for 30 days, then enable for all services
Rollback: Flip feature flag to disable quarantine and priority drain; autoscaler rules revert to previous behavior
test_plan: Unit tests: readiness controller state transitions, TTL and backoff logic
Integration tests: router respects quarantine metadata and routes only allowed priority buckets
Chaos: kernel pause, GC spike, simulated probe flaps to verify quarantine engages and autoscaler does not thrash
Load test: synthetic P95/P99 latency under mixed priority traffic with 20% of nodes quarantined
Canary metrics: compare scale event rate and SLO violations vs baseline for 14 days
